newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH PORK EXPORTS WORTH NLG 5.1 BLN IN 1996.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH PORK EXPORTS WORTH NLG 5.1 BLN IN 1996.

text.p: The Netherlands exported pigs and pork products worth some 5.1 billion guilders in 1996, an 11 percent increase compared with 1995, the Central Bureau of Statistics (CBS) said on Wednesday.
This figure is a full-year estimate, extrapolated from an 11 percent increase in exports in the first nine months of 1996.
The CBS said the Netherlands produced 1,624 million kilograms of pigs and pork products in 1996 of which about 60 percent was exported.
The European Union's Standing Veterinary Committee is meeting today to discuss an outbreak of swine fever in the Netherlands and Germany.
The Netherlands export pigs or pork products to all EU countries, and the value of exports to other EU member states is estimated at 4.8 billion guilders in 1996.
In 1995, Germany bought 38 percent of total Dutch pig and pork exports, Italy 22 percent and Britain 11 percent.
The CBS said there were an estimated 14.2 million pigs in the Netherlands in December 1996, a two percent increase compared with a year earlier.
According to a survey held last May one fifth of all pigs in the Netherlands are located in the "Westelijk Peelgebied" area of the southern Netherlands where swine fever has broken out.
Swine fever, last detected in the Netherlands in 1992, is a highly contagious disease but it is not harmful to humans.
The outbreak has so far been confined to a relatively small area in the province of North Brabant and the government hopes its seclusion policy will be sufficient to contain the disease.

The Dutch authorities, anxious to prevent restrictions of key pork exports, have decided to slaughter all pigs at 26 farms in the area immediately surrounding the first case -- discovered last week. An estimated 30,000 are expected to be killed.
The United States said on Tuesday it was banning imports of pork products from the Netherlands because of the swine fever infection. Poland has also banned imports.
